findings.title: Description issues instructions to the model
findings.detail: Description of "request_upload" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: request_upload, convert_statement, get_statement, list_outflows · Private data: request_upload, convert_statement, get_statement, categorize_statement, dismiss_statement, adjudicate_outflows, get_credits, rate_statement, list_transactions, group_by, list_outflows · Public sink: request_upload, get_statement, get_credits, rate_statement · Destructive: categorize_statement, dismiss_statement.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: request_upload, convert_statement, get_statement, list_outflows · Private data: request_upload, convert_statement, get_statement, categorize_statement, dismiss_statement, adjudicate_outflows, get_credits, rate_statement, list_transactions, group_by, list_outflows · Public sink: request_upload, get_statement, get_credits, rate_statement · Destructive: categorize_statement, dismiss_statement

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
